SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 8.2.1 Fluency, part of Domestic animals Suggested vocabulary pasture, hay, water, donkey, goat, meat, m in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read fluently? 2. Why do we pause when we read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Identify words with the target letter-sound combinations (- ft, -ct, -lt, -rd). Learners with speech difficulties can identify orally, by typing or writing.
2. Read words with the target letter-sound combinations.
3. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.
4. Read a text, displaying the right facial expressions and tone

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Collaboration: Team work is enhanced as the learner participates in group activities observing the rules of engagement.

Values:
Peace: Care is developed as the learner displays tolerance with peers during group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Socio-economic issues (Animal Welfare Education): The learner acquires information on how to take care of domestic

animals as they recite poems on care of animals.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the reading fluency skills learnt as they read texts in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Sample poems, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners,
